newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to review role in Nazi victims' funds - report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to review role in Nazi victims' funds - report.

text.p: The Clinton administration has agreed to review whether the U.S. government unfairly confiscated funds deposited in New York banks by European Jews who may have perished in the Holocaust, the Washington Post reported on Sunday.

The United States, which has urged Switzerland to resolve the ownership of Swiss bank accounts dormant since the Second World War, will also examine the question of "heirless" accounts in U.S. banks as part of an interagency study on financial assets looted by the Nazis or left behind by war victims, the newspaper said.

"If we are going to shine the spotlight of history on the role of other countries, then we have an equal obligation to be willing to shine the spotlight of history on our own involvement," Commerce Undersecretary Stuart Eizenstat told the Post in an interview.

Jewish organisations and U.S. officials have pressed Switzerland and other countries that remained neutral during the Second World War to make a full accounting of unclaimed money belonging to Holocaust victims.
Swiss banks, in particular, have been accused of reaping a multi-billion dollar windfall since victims often left no heirs or heirs who had trouble proving a claim to the accounts.
The study headed by Eizenstat is scheduled for release next month, the Post reported.
